body: Stop renting your intelligence. Own it with AnythingLLM. Everything you need for a powerful local-first agent experience
plain_description: AnythingLLM gives you a private AI assistant without monthly per-seat fees or vendor lock-in. Chat with your documents, automate complex workflows with AI agents, and deploy on your own terms—locally, in Docker, or in the cloud. Set up in minutes, scale as you grow.
technical_description: AnythingLLM is an open-source, local-first AI application platform that provides a complete alternative to managed AI services. The monorepo consists of a Node.js/Express API server, a React/ViteJS frontend, and a separate document collector service. It supports a wide range of LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Ollama, LM Studio, and 30+ others), embedding models, and vector databases (LanceDB, PGVector, Pinecone, Chroma, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus). Core capabilities include RAG-based document chat, AI agent workflows with MCP compatibility, multi-user access control with role-based permissions, scheduled job execution, model routing, and a full REST API for custom integrations. The application can be deployed via Docker, Kubernetes, bare metal, or cloud platforms, and desktop clients are available for Mac, Windows, and Linux.
title: AnythingLLM

plain_description: Chatbox is your all-in-one AI copilot that brings ChatGPT, Claude, and other leading LLMs straight to your desktop. No complex setup needed — just download, configure your provider, and start chatting. Your data stays on your device, keeping every conversation private and secure.
technical_description: Chatbox is an Electron-based desktop application (TypeScript, React) that provides a unified client interface for multiple large language model providers including OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Claude, Google Gemini Pro, Ollama, and ChatGLM-6B. It features local-first data storage, streaming reply rendering, Markdown and LaTeX display with syntax highlighting, keyboard shortcuts, dark theme support, and internationalization across 10+ locales. The application is distributed as native desktop installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux, with companion iOS and Android mobile apps and a web version. The Community Edition is open-sourced under GPLv3 with code regularly synced from the proprietary Pro version.
title: Chatbox

body: GPT4All: Run Local LLMs on Any Device. Open-source and available for commercial use.
plain_description: GPT4All lets you run powerful AI chatbots entirely on your own computer — no internet connection, cloud fees, or GPU required. Your data stays private on your machine with no API calls ever sent to third parties. The bottom line: enterprise-grade LLM capabilities at zero recurring cost, with full commercial use rights.
technical_description: GPT4All is an open-source ecosystem for local inference of large language models on consumer hardware. It provides a cross-platform desktop chat application (Windows, macOS, Linux), Python bindings wrapping llama.cpp for GGUF-format models, and a Docker-based OpenAI-compatible HTTP API server. The project supports CPU-only inference plus GPU acceleration via Nomic Vulkan on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, with optimized performance on Apple Silicon. LocalDocs enables retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) by indexing local files for private, offline document chat.
title: GPT4All

body: The open source codebase powering HuggingChat
plain_description: Deploy a production-ready AI chat interface in minutes — the same open-source engine that powers HuggingChat. Connect it to any OpenAI-compatible provider and give your team a polished web chat experience with no vendor lock-in. MCP tool support, smart model routing, and customizable branding included.
technical_description: Chat UI is a SvelteKit web application that provides a browser-based chat interface for large language models. It communicates exclusively through OpenAI-compatible REST API endpoints (/v1/chat/completions, /models), supporting any backend that implements this protocol — including llama.cpp server, Ollama, OpenRouter, and Hugging Face Inference Providers. Data persistence (conversation history, user settings, files, and statistics) uses MongoDB, with an embedded fallback for local development. The application includes an optional heuristic-based LLM Router for model selection, MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool support via OpenAI function calling, and environment-variable-driven theming. Deployment options include bare metal (npm), Docker (ghcr.io/huggingface/chat-ui-db), or any SvelteKit adapter for cloud platforms.
title: Chat UI

body: Jan is an open source alternative to ChatGPT that runs 100% offline on your computer.
plain_description: Jan gives you a powerful AI assistant that runs completely offline on your computer — no data ever leaves your machine. It works like ChatGPT but keeps your conversations private and under your control. The bottom line: full AI capability with zero privacy compromises.
technical_description: Jan is an open-source desktop application for running large language models locally, built with TypeScript and Rust on the Tauri framework. It supports local inference through llama.cpp (GGUF format) and MLX backends with hardware acceleration for CPU, NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon GPUs. The application exposes an OpenAI-compatible REST API at localhost:1337 for integration with external tools, includes RAG capabilities via a vector database extension, and supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) for agentic workflows. Remote model providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, and MiniMax are available as optional cloud integrations.
title: Jan

plain_description: LibreChat gives you one self-hosted platform to unify every major AI model under a single, privacy-controlled interface. Your team gets a ChatGPT-like experience for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and dozens of other providers — no more juggling tabs or exposing data to third parties. You control the infrastructure, your users get a seamless AI assistant.
technical_description: LibreChat is an open-source, self-hosted AI chat platform built on Node.js/TypeScript with a React client. It provides a unified API gateway to 20+ AI providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and local models via Ollama. The architecture consists of a Node.js REST API server, a React frontend with multilingual support, MongoDB for persistence, and optional Redis for resumable streams and horizontal scaling. Key capabilities include multi-user authentication (OAuth2, LDAP, email), role-based access control, a browser-based admin panel, customizable AI agents with MCP tool integration, a sandboxed code interpreter supporting multiple languages, generative UI artifacts, and searchable conversation history.
title: LibreChat

body: llama and other  large language models on iOS and MacOS offline using GGML library.
plain_description: The big picture: Run powerful AI language models directly on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac — completely offline with no internet connection needed. Here's why it matters: You can test, compare, and run dozens of models privately on your own device without sending data to the cloud. The bottom line: private, on-device AI that works anywhere.
technical_description: LLMFarm is a native iOS and macOS application for running large language models (LLMs) locally using the ggml library and llama.cpp. It supports multiple model architectures including LLaMA, Gemma, Phi, Falcon, Mamba, RWKV, and multimodal models such as LLaVA and BakLLaVA. Inference is accelerated via Metal on Apple Silicon and runs entirely on-device with no cloud dependency. The application provides configurable sampling methods (temperature, top-k, top-p, tail-free sampling, Mirostat, grammar-based sampling), persistent context state management, Apple Shortcuts integration, and a built-in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system. Models are loaded in GGML and GGUF formats.
title: LLMFarm

body: 🤯 LobeHub is your Chief Agent Operator, organizing your agents into 7×24 operations by hiring, scheduling, and reporting on your entire AI team.
plain_description: LobeHub is your Chief Agent Operator — it hires, schedules, and reports on your entire AI team so you stay in charge without staying online. The big picture: treat agents as the unit of work, bringing all your AI teammates under one roof with shared context, personal memory, and scheduled runs. The bottom line: more productivity, fewer tools, and agents that learn from how you work.
technical_description: LobeHub is an open-source multi-agent orchestration platform that treats agents as the unit of work. It provides a full-stack architecture with a Next.js + Vite SPA frontend and a Hono-based server backend. The platform supports agent creation via an Agent Builder, agent groups for parallel collaboration, personal memory with structured white-box storage, scheduled task execution, and an IM Gateway for multi-platform messaging (Discord, Slack, Telegram, WeChat, etc.). It exposes a REST API and integrates with over 10,000 tools and MCP-compatible plugins. Deployment options include Docker, Vercel, Zeabur, Sealos, Alibaba Cloud, and bare metal.
title: LobeHub

body: User-friendly AI Interface (Supports Ollama, OpenAI API, ...)
plain_description: Open WebUI is a self-hosted AI platform that gives your organization complete control over AI interactions while keeping all data private and offline. It connects to any major AI model provider—local or cloud—in a single unified interface. The bottom line: one platform for chat, document search, image generation, voice, and team collaboration without sending data to third parties.
technical_description: Open WebUI is a self-hosted AI frontend and platform written in Python (FastAPI backend) and Svelte (frontend). It supports any OpenAI-compatible API provider alongside local Ollama deployments, with a built-in RAG inference engine backed by nine vector database options (ChromaDB, PGVector, Qdrant, Milvus, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Pinecone, S3Vector, Oracle 23ai). The platform exposes a REST API, an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint, and a WebSocket interface for real-time features. Deployment is available via pip, Docker (with :ollama and :cuda tags), or Kubernetes (kubectl, kustomize, helm). It includes plugin architecture (Filters, Actions, Pipes, Tools, Skills), MCP/MCPO tool server support, RBAC with LDAP/SSO/SCIM 2.0, persistent memory, web search for RAG, multi-model conversations, image generation (DALL-E, Gemini, ComfyUI, AUTOMATIC1111), voice/video calls with multiple STT/TTS providers, and a PWA for mobile access.
title: Open WebUI

body: An app that brings language models directly to your phone.
plain_description: Run a private AI assistant entirely on your phone — no account, no cloud, no internet required. Your conversations, documents, and voice data never leave your device. Free and open source with no subscription or 'pro' tier.
technical_description: PocketPal AI is a React Native mobile application that runs large language models and text-to-speech models entirely on-device via local inference, with no network connection required after setup. It employs a four-layer architecture: React Native UI with MobX state management and WatermelonDB persistence; native bridging through llama.rn and react-native-speech; inference engines llama.cpp for GGUF-quantized LLMs and ONNX Runtime for TTS models; and hardware acceleration targeting CPU, GPU (Metal on iOS), and NPU (Qualcomm Hexagon). The AgentRunner drives a tool-use loop that enables Talents (calculator, datetime, HTML rendering) for agentic capabilities. Models are downloaded from Hugging Face or local storage and selected by quantization level to fit device memory.
title: PocketPal AI

plain_description: SillyTavern is a single, powerful interface that lets you chat with any major AI model, generate images, and add voice to conversations — all without switching between tools. It runs entirely on your own machine, keeping your data private and giving you full control over how you use AI. The bottom line: one app, every leading AI provider, no cloud lock-in.
technical_description: SillyTavern is a self-hosted, web-based frontend application that provides a unified interface for interacting with large language models (LLMs), image generation engines, and text-to-speech services. Built on Node.js 20+, it serves a responsive HTML/JavaScript client with backend connectors for KoboldAI, KoboldCPP, Horde, NovelAI, Ooba, Tabby, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Anthropic Claude, and Mistral. The application includes a plugin-based extension system, lorebook (WorldInfo) management, auto-translation, Visual Novel Mode, and integration with Automatic1111 and ComfyUI for image generation. It can be deployed via Docker or installed directly on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android (Termux).
title: SillyTavern

body: Open-source desktop app for local LLMs. Text, vision, tool-calling, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API. 100% private.
plain_description: Run powerful AI chatbots, image generators, and document analyzers entirely on your own computer with no data ever leaving your machine. Replace cloud subscriptions with a free, open-source desktop app that works offline, supports private file analysis, and connects to any OpenAI-compatible tool you already use. No telemetry, no account, no ongoing costs.
technical_description: TextGen is an open-source inference server and desktop application for running large language models on local hardware. It supports multiple inference backends—llama.cpp (GGUF), ExLlamaV3, Hugging Face Transformers (PyTorch), and TensorRT-LLM—with runtime backend switching and model hot-swapping without restart. The application exposes a Gradio-based web interface for chat, instruction-following, and notebook-style generation, plus an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible REST API providing Chat, Completions, and Messages endpoints with tool-calling and MCP server support. Additional capabilities include multimodal vision via mmproj files, document ingestion (PDF, DOCX, plain text), image generation via diffusers with 4-bit/8-bit quantization, LoRA fine-tuning on multi-turn chat or raw text datasets, and an extension system for TTS, STT, web search, and translation. Deployment options include portable builds bundling all dependencies for Linux, Windows, and macOS with CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, or CPU-only configurations, as well as Docker Compose and manual Python environment setups.
title: TextGen
